name: Dice
note: Pick a number, pick over or under, set your own win chance.
steps: Set a target number between 0 and 100 — this sets both your win chance and your multiplier.
Choose whether the roll must land over or under it.
Stake and roll. The result is derived from a server seed, your client seed and a nonce.
Verify any roll afterwards by re-hashing the seed triplet in the fairness tab.
tips: Nothing you do changes the edge. Casinos publish their own figure, and the ones we found are listed below.
Martingale-style auto-bet setups lose to the table limit, not to the edge. The limit always arrives first.
Auto-bet with a stop-loss is the only setting on this game worth configuring.

name: Crash
note: A multiplier climbs from 1× and busts at a random point. Cash out first.
steps: Place your stake before the round starts — bets lock when the curve begins.
Watch the multiplier climb from 1.00×.
Cash out before it busts; your return is stake × the multiplier at that moment.
Set an auto-cashout target if you would rather not decide under pressure.
tips: A 2× auto-cashout wins roughly half the time. That is the whole game — there is no read on the curve.
Previous rounds are independent. A long red streak tells you nothing about the next round.
Partial cashouts, where offered, are the only genuine risk-management tool here.

name: Plinko
note: A ball falls through pins into a multiplier bucket. Pick your risk row.
steps: Choose a risk level — low, medium or high — and the number of rows.
Drop the ball. Its path is determined by the seed triplet, not by physics.
The bucket it lands in sets your multiplier.
Higher risk widens the buckets at both ends without changing the edge.
tips: Risk level changes variance only. Expected return is identical across all three.
High risk with the most rows gives the longest dry spells.
The centre buckets pay under 1×, which is where most of your rounds land.

name: Mines
note: Reveal safe tiles on a grid, avoid the mines, cash out when you like.
steps: Choose how many mines to hide on the 5×5 grid — more mines, higher multiplier per tile.
Reveal tiles one at a time. Each safe tile increases your multiplier.
Cash out at any point, or keep going and risk the lot.
The mine layout is fixed at round start and provable afterwards.
tips: With three mines, four safe picks pays about 1.7× at a 1% edge. More mines raise the multiplier and the risk together.
The multiplier curve accelerates late, which is exactly when the risk per tile is highest.
Because you choose when to stop, it suits a fixed session target.

name: Limbo
note: Set a target multiplier; win if the round rolls above it.
steps: Enter a target multiplier — the higher it is, the lower your win chance.
Stake and roll.
If the round result exceeds your target, you win stake × target.
The win chance is shown before you commit, so the maths is never hidden.
tips: A 100× target wins roughly once in a hundred rolls. It will feel much rarer than that.
This is Dice with the interface stripped back; casinos usually publish the same edge for both.
Useful for a single high-multiplier shot, poor for grinding.

name: Keno
note: Pick numbers on a grid and see how many the draw matches.
steps: Select between one and ten numbers on the grid (40 numbers on most originals versions).
Choose a risk level, which reshapes the payout table.
Draw. Numbers are pulled (ten on most versions) and your matches set the multiplier.
The paytable is shown live as you pick, so you can see what each hit is worth.
tips: Picking more numbers does not improve your edge — it just flattens the payout curve.
At high risk, low match counts pay nothing at all. Read the table before staking.
The slowest-feeling of the instant originals, despite resolving immediately.

name: Hi-Lo
note: Guess whether the next card is higher or lower. Build a streak.
steps: A card is dealt face up.
Call the next card higher or lower — the odds shown reflect the remaining deck.
Each correct call compounds your multiplier.
Cash out whenever, or lose the streak on a wrong call.
tips: Calling the obvious side of a 2 or a King is close to a free step, and the multiplier reflects that.
The compounding is what makes this dangerous — five correct calls feel like a system.
Same-rank ties are handled differently between operators. Check before you play.

name: Wheel
note: A segmented wheel spins into a multiplier. Pick risk and segment count.
steps: Choose risk level and how many segments the wheel carries.
Stake before the spin.
The wheel lands on a segment and pays its multiplier.
Segment layout and result are both verifiable after the round.
tips: Low risk pays under 2× on almost every segment; high risk pays nothing on most of them.
Segment count changes granularity, not edge.
The most passive game in the lobby — nothing to decide once the stake is set.
